mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) from the prior month to the current month consistently compresses equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as lower rates reduce the cost of capital for equity valuation.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1 percentage points from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer spending power and economic uncertainty.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE rises by at least 0.2 percentage points from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 0.5% and fall in industrial production (INDPRO) below 0.5% within one month signals sectoral misalignment between consumer demand and manufacturing output, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate economic weakness.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 0.5% and INDPRO falls > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 40% of instances where HOUST rises by at least 0.5% and INDPRO falls by at least 0.5% from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a monthly CPI increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals inflationary pressures that prompt aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as discount rates rise for equity valuations.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 40% of instances during late-cycle expansions when CPIAUCSL rises by at least 0.3 percentage points from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the prior month consistently correlates with stronger consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved household income and economic confidence.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 40% of months where PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals accelerating inflation that triggers immediate market concern about central bank tightening, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises by at least 0.3 percentage points from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of a federal funds rate decline exceeding 0.1 percentage points and unemployment rate above 5.0% signals active monetary policy response to economic weakness, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate stabilization.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1 percentage points and UNRATE exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: During industrial production slowdowns (INDPRO falling below 100), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days as manufacturing weakness signals broader economic contraction and reduced corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO falls below 100.
